chunks: Abu Abdillah al-Ash'ari, from al-Sayyari, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Karkhi, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When a man enters a city, he is a guest upon those in it from the people of his religion, until he departs from them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hospitality for a traveler entering a new city?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the communal obligation of hospitality (diyafah) in Shia jurisprudence, framing the traveler not merely as a visitor but as a temporary member of the local religious community. It reflects the broader Islamic principle of social solidarity, where the host's duty extends until the guest's departure, reinforcing the bonds of brotherhood (ukhuwwah) within the Ummah.
